key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within minutes. LOCATION: UNILATERAL weakness, numbness, or paralysis. DURATION: SYMPTOMS RESOLVE within 24 hours (usually within minutes to hours). CHARACTER: SUDDEN, SEVERE weakness, numbness, or paralysis that RESOLVES. AGGRAVATING: MOVEMENT, speaking, swallowing. RELIEVING: SYMPTOMS RESOLVE spontaneously. TIMING: Sudden onset, symptoms resolve within 24 hours. SEVERITY: 6-8/10 during episode, then resolves. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: FACIAL DROOP, arm weakness, speech difficulty, vision problems, dizziness, confusion, headache. KEY POSITIVES: Positive FAST test (Face, Arm, Speech, Time), unilateral weakness, facial droop, speech difficulty. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no photophobia.

red_flags: Symptoms lasting >24 hours - possible stroke, call 911
Severe neurological deficits with altered mental status - possible stroke, call 911
Signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
